prompt.context_jp: 甘春総合病院の廊下に、一着の白衣___掲げられていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 甘春総合病院の廊下に、一着の白衣___掲げられていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces the white coat as new information in the scene.

feedback.correct_en: The white coat is being introduced for the first time as new information in the opening scene, so が marks it as the newly presented subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the coat is already a known topic. を would require a transitive verb, but 掲げられていた is passive here.

contrast_examples.en: There is a white coat in the hallway. (new info)
That white coat (already known) is famous.

prompt.context_jp: マッチングアプリで知り合った相手からのメッセージ___、彼の目に痛々しく映る。
prompt.prompt_jp: マッチングアプリで知り合った相手からのメッセージ___、彼の目に痛々しく映る。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the newly introduced message as subject.

feedback.correct_en: The message is newly introduced in the scene and acts as the subject appearing in his vision. が marks this new, specific subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the message as a pre-established topic, which doesn't fit this descriptive moment.

contrast_examples.jp: メッセージは短かった。

prompt.context_jp: 初めての一人当直という重圧___、まだ経験の浅い彼女の胸を確かに侵している。
prompt.prompt_jp: 初めての一人当直という重圧___、まだ経験の浅い彼女の胸を確かに侵している。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 重圧 as the subject exerting pressure on her?

feedback.correct_en: The pressure is the active agent 'invading' her heart — newly described, specific subject. が is natural here.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it an abstract topic statement, losing the immediacy of the moment. に is a location/direction marker, not subject.

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐: 「恋愛なんて時間の無駄です」軒下: 「お前___一生 機械 いじってろ」
prompt.prompt_jp: お前___一生 機械 いじってろ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that establishes 'you' as the topic of the command.

feedback.correct_en: Nokishita is making a statement about Igarashi (as topic/contrast): 'As for you, just play with machines forever.' は is the topic/contrastive marker.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce お前 as new info or emphasize exhaustivity, neither fits this teasing retort.

prompt.context_jp: それでも五十嵐の眼差し___、静かな確信に満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: それでも五十嵐の眼差し___、静かな確信に満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits as topic marker here (with contrastive それでも)?

feedback.correct_en: それでも signals a contrast: unlike Nokishita's dismissiveness, 'as for Igarashi's gaze, it was full of conviction.' は carries that contrastive topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce new information, but Igarashi is already the topical figure being contrasted against the prior sentence.

contrast_examples.en: His eyes, by contrast, were serious.

prompt.context_jp: 会計を終えて廊下に出た真貴___、通りすがりに白衣姿の男を見上げて息をのんだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 真貴___、通りすがりに白衣姿の男を見上げて息をのんだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Maki as the ongoing narrative topic here?

feedback.correct_en: Maki has already been established; this sentence continues the narrative about her and describes what she did. は marks her as the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present her as newly introduced, but she's been in the scene since the prior sentences.

prompt.context_jp: そこにいたの___、中学時代、密かに憧れていた同級生の面影を残す男だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: そこにいたの___、中学時代、密かに憧れていた同級生の面影を残す男だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this cleft-like 'the one who was there was…' construction?

feedback.correct_en: The structure そこにいたのは〜だった is a topic-comment cleft: 'As for who was there, it was…' は is standard here.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly re-introduce the one-who-was-there as new info, but the pattern のは…だった identifies a known referent.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が好きなのはこれだ。

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐: 「う～ん… ___がよくありません しかも 大きい 悪性の可能性が高いと思います」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___がよくありません
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits? (Igarashi describing the appearance of a lump on imaging)

feedback.correct_en: 顔つき is used metaphorically in radiology to mean the 'look/features' of a lesion on imaging. It's the canonical collocation here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 顔色 ('complexion') and 表情 ('facial expression') refer to actual faces, not lesion morphology on scans.

contrast_examples.jp: この腫瘤は顔つきが悪い。
contrast_examples.en: This mass has bad features (looks malignant).

prompt.context_jp: 杏: 「彼は 意見を言ってるだけで 判断___私が行っています」
prompt.prompt_jp: 判断___私が行っています
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle makes 'the decision' the contrastive topic (vs. opinion)?

feedback.correct_en: An contrasts two things: 'As for his role, it's giving opinions; as for the decision (判断), I make it.' は marks 判断 as the contrastive topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would make 判断 a simple object, losing the contrast. が would put emphasis on 判断 as new info, but the contrastive framing is what she needs.

prompt.context_jp: 鏑木: 「そして 彼___我々 医師を 全く信頼していません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼___我々 医師を 全く信頼していません
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'he' as the topic Kaburaki is making a sweeping claim about?

feedback.correct_en: Kaburaki is making a generalization about Igarashi ('as for him, he doesn't trust us doctors'). は marks the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal new information or exhaustive identification, but here Igarashi is already the known referent of the complaint.

contrast_examples.en: He is the one who doesn't trust. (exhaustive)

prompt.context_jp: 鏑木: 「医師免許を持たない者が 医業をしてはならない 医師法第17条 ___ですね？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 医師法第17条 ___ですね？
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrase fits as Kaburaki's pointed 'you know it, right?'

feedback.correct_en: ご存じ is the respectful form of 知っている, appropriate for Kaburaki's formally cutting tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 知ってる is too casual for this confrontational-but-formal register. わかる means 'understand', not 'know of'.

prompt.context_jp: 軒下: 「中学の同級生だからって ___はできないよ 悪いな」
prompt.prompt_jp: 中学の同級生だからって ___はできないよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which expression fits — Nokishita refusing to give his old friend preferential treatment?

feedback.correct_en: 特別扱いはできない ('I can't give special treatment') is the exact collocation for this ethical refusal.
feedback.incorrect_en: 特別料金 (special pricing) and 特別注文 (special order) make no sense for medical examination priority.

contrast_examples.jp: 特別扱いはできません。
特別な配慮をお願いします。

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐: 「このケースは いわゆる___といって 日本の医療の現状では 残念ながら 今すぐ どうにかできる問題では ないんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: いわゆる___といって
prompt.prompt_en: Which term describes patients stuck waiting for screening/diagnosis?

feedback.correct_en: 検診難民 ('screening refugee') is the specific term for patients unable to get timely re-examination.
feedback.incorrect_en: 医療事故 is a medical accident; 過剰診療 is over-treatment. Neither describes the waiting-list problem Igarashi explains.

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐: 「とにかく 今は冷静になって 奥様を___あげることが 何よりも大切です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 奥様を___あげることが
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits — what the husband can do for his wife right now?

feedback.correct_en: 支える ('to support') is the natural verb for emotional support during illness — matches Igarashi's gentle counsel.
feedback.incorrect_en: 育てる (raise/nurture) implies child-rearing. 守る (protect) is possible but less fitting — the issue is emotional support through waiting, not protection from a threat.

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐: 「蛭田さん 精神的に 随分と 追い詰められてるみたいで なるべく早く はっきりとした 診断___してあげてほしいんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: はっきりとした 診断___してあげてほしい
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 診断 as the direct object of する?

feedback.correct_en: 診断する ('to make a diagnosis') takes を for the direct object noun.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as subject, which doesn't fit a request directed at the doctor. に is directional/locational.

prompt.context_jp: 大森: 「甘春先生の言うとおりね 病院として___ 個人的な感情だけで 一部の患者を優遇するわけには いかないわ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 病院として___
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'as a hospital' as the framing topic?

feedback.correct_en: 〜としては sets up a framing/perspective topic: 'Speaking from the hospital's standpoint...' は is standard with として in this topicalizing use.
feedback.incorrect_en: が wouldn't work as a perspective frame. で alone would mean 'at/by' but loses the contrastive framing.

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐: 「悪性の可能性___あります カテゴリー4 もしくは 5 構築の乱れ___見られます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 悪性の可能性___あります
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in 'there is a possibility of malignancy'?

feedback.correct_en: The existential pattern 〜がある presents new information: 'there is a possibility.' が is required.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose that possibility is an established topic. を can't mark the subject of ある.

contrast_examples.en: As for time, I have some. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 軒下: 「クソ… 結局 検査じゃ 患者 ___えねえか 技師って何なんだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 検査じゃ 患者 ___えねえか
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits Nokishita's frustrated line about what exams can do for patients?

feedback.correct_en: 救えねえ (=救えない, 'can't save') captures his frustration that exams alone can't save patients.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見えねえ ('can't see') and 治えねえ (not a real conjugation — 治す is used) don't fit the context of helplessness he's expressing.

prompt.context_jp: 軒下: 「この出会いが人生を左右する ほどのものだったとしても 遠慮___ いらないからな」
prompt.prompt_jp: 遠慮___ いらない
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 遠慮 contrastively in 'no need to hold back'?

feedback.correct_en: 遠慮はいらない is a set phrase ('no need to hold back'), where は gives contrastive/emphatic negation — 'holding back, no need for that.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 遠慮がいらない sounds unnatural here; the idiomatic form uses は for the implicit contrast with other options.

prompt.context_jp: 杏: 「患者さんより自分___優先なんです あの人は」
prompt.prompt_jp: 患者さんより自分___優先なんです
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits — exhaustive 'himself' as what he prioritizes?

feedback.correct_en: 'Himself (not patients) is the priority' — が emphasizes the exhaustive identification: of the two, 自分 is what's prioritized.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would weaken the sharp contrast An is drawing. を would require a different verb.

prompt.context_jp: 杏: 「最近 自分の診断___ 自信が持てなくて」
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の診断___ 自信が持てなくて
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits — 'can't have confidence in my own diagnoses'?

feedback.correct_en: 自信を持つ takes に for the target of the confidence: '〜に自信を持つ' ('have confidence in 〜').
feedback.incorrect_en: を would need another object. が would conflict with 自信が, which already takes が.

prompt.context_jp: 軒下 confessing to Yuka that he's not actually a doctor.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Nokishita's confession?

choices.text: ごめんなさい。病院で働いてるけど、医師免許は持ってないんだ。
ごめんなさい。病院で働いてるけど、医師免許が持ってないんだ。
ごめんなさい。病院に働いてるけど、医師免許は持ってないんだ。

feedback.correct_en: 医師免許は持ってない uses は for contrastive negation ('a license — that I don't have'). 病院で働く uses で for location of action.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses が before a negated 持つ, which is awkward — は is standard with negation of possession. C uses 病院に働く, but 働く takes で for workplace.

prompt.context_jp: 軒下 teaching Hirose how to assess the patient.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is most natural for 'don't be fooled by appearances'?

choices.text: 見た目に惑わされんな。大事なのは観察だ。
見た目が惑わされんな。大事なのは観察だ。
見た目を惑わされんな。大事なのは観察だ。

feedback.correct_en: 惑わされる (passive of 惑わす) takes に to mark the cause/agent: 'be misled by appearances.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 見た目 the subject being misled, which is nonsensical. を doesn't fit passive here.

prompt.context_jp: 鏑木 lecturing about what trust means.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for 'respect each other'?

choices.text: それぞれの役割に責任を持ち、互いに尊重し合うこと。
それぞれの役割を責任を持ち、互いに尊重し合うこと。
それぞれの役割に責任が持ち、互いに尊重し合うこと。

feedback.correct_en: 責任を持つ ('bear responsibility') takes を, and the thing one is responsible for is marked with に: 役割に責任を持つ.
feedback.incorrect_en: B stacks two を, which is ungrammatical. C uses が incorrectly before 持つ (which is transitive and takes を).

prompt.context_jp: 蛭田: 「妻とは幼なじみで ずっと 彼女のこと___好きで…」
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女のこと___好きで
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle completes Hiruta's confession 'I've liked her all along'?

feedback.correct_en: 好き is an adjectival noun (na-adjective); its object is marked with が: 〜が好きだ.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is often heard colloquially with 好き but is non-standard. に doesn't fit the pattern.

prompt.context_jp: Narrator introducing the story's theme.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version is most natural as a narrative opening?

choices.text: この物語は、その白衣に憧れ、あるいは重荷を感じる者たちの日常から始まる。
この物語が、その白衣に憧れ、あるいは重荷を感じる者たちの日常から始まる。
この物語を、その白衣に憧れ、あるいは重荷を感じる者たちの日常から始まる。

feedback.correct_en: この物語は〜から始まる uses は because 'this story' is the overarching topic being introduced to the audience.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly treat the story as new/exhaustive info in a generic opening. を doesn't fit the intransitive 始まる.

contrast_examples.en: A story is about to start. (new event)

prompt.context_jp: Nokishita's quip about charming women.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for his cocky line?

choices.text: 女 口説くのに酒はいらねえ。ブドウジュースで十分だ。
女 口説くのに酒がいらねえ。ブドウジュースで十分だ。
女 口説くのに酒をいらねえ。ブドウジュースで十分だ。

feedback.correct_en: 酒はいらない uses は for contrastive negation — 'alcohol? I don't need any (grape juice is enough).' This matches the boastful contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would weaken the contrast with ブドウジュース. を doesn't work with いる ('need'), which takes が/は for the needed item.

contrast_examples.en: I don't need sugar. (contrast with other options)
